meta.title: tezera Platform Architecture (ATP release, no ticketing)
meta.subtitle: Mobile app and web portal for organisers, providers and consumers

boundaries.label: Backend · TypeScript on free tiers (Render, Neon, Upstash)

cards.title: Where it runs: why, and alternatives
items: Vercel (web portal). Why: made by the Next.js team, so deploys need no setup; a preview link for every pull request; pages served from its edge network; free Hobby tier. Alternatives: Netlify, Cloudflare Pages.

Render (API and job worker). Why: runs long-lived Node processes, which SSE streams and BullMQ workers need (serverless functions time out); deploys from GitHub; free tier. Watch: free instances sleep when idle, so the first request after a pause is slow. Alternatives: Railway, Fly.io, Koyeb.
Neon (PostgreSQL). Why: managed Postgres with a free tier and database branches for testing; works with Prisma. Alternatives: Supabase, Render Postgres, Aiven.

Upstash (Redis). Why: managed Redis billed per request, with a free tier; carries BullMQ jobs and the SSE pub/sub. Watch: BullMQ polls Redis often, so check usage against the free limit. Alternatives: Redis Cloud, Render Key Value.

Cloudinary (media CDN). Why: stores images, reels, layouts and private verification documents, resizes and compresses on request, and serves the app and the web portal from one CDN; free tier. Alternatives: Cloudflare R2 with Cloudflare Images, AWS S3 with CloudFront, Bunny.net.

cards.title: Services and protocols: why, and alternatives
items: SSE instead of WebSockets. Why: one-way server-to-client updates over plain HTTPS, with automatic reconnect, that pass through proxies easily; sending a message stays a REST call. The mobile app needs a small SSE library (for example react-native-sse). Alternatives: Socket.IO or raw WebSockets, polling, Ably or Pusher.

Expo (EAS Build and Expo Push). Why: one React Native codebase for Android and iOS, cloud builds without a Mac, one push API over FCM and APNs. Alternatives: bare React Native with Firebase Cloud Messaging, OneSignal.
Resend (email). Why: simple API, free tier, email templates written in React. Alternatives: Amazon SES, Brevo, Postmark.

Dialog e-SMS (OTP and urgent alerts). Why: a Sri Lankan operator's own gateway, with sender ID masking, delivery reports and billing in LKR. Watch: needs a Dialog Enterprise account and its API documentation is thin, so test early. Alternatives: Notify.lk, Twilio, other local bulk-SMS gateways.

cards.title: Recommended stack
items: One TypeScript monorepo (Turborepo) with shared types and Zod validation
Mobile: React Native + Expo, one app for all four roles with role-based navigation
Web: Next.js portal for every role, consumers included, plus a role-gated admin panel
Backend: NestJS modular monolith on Prisma and PostgreSQL; REST for requests, Server-Sent Events (SSE) for live updates
Live updates: each client keeps one SSE stream open; Redis pub/sub passes events between API instances

cards.title: Interactive 2D venue map
items: Organisers upload a layout image, drop pins and draw named zones as boxes, e.g. 'Food court'
Consumers tap a zone to see its stalls; each stall shows the vendor, items and prices in LKR
Search by item (e.g. 'kottu') highlights matching stalls; 'Find on map' jumps to a stall
One map record (pins, zones) stored as JSON in PostgreSQL; zones kept as fractions of the layout so they scale (proposed)
Drawn as an SVG overlay on the layout: react-native-svg in the app, SVG in Next.js
Stall items in their own table, included in PostgreSQL text search
Mobile app only: keeps an opened event's map, times and announcements offline, with a 'last updated' time (Could)

cards.title: API modules
items: Accounts, profiles and verification
Events and promotion feed (posts, reels)
Hiring marketplace: direct bookings, job posts, quotes, stalls
Reviews and ranking (weighted rank score, badges, leaderboards); search via PostgreSQL text search + pg_trgm
Venue maps: layout, pins, zones, stall items and prices
Community boards, meetups, messaging, announcements
Admin: verification, report queue, disputes, audit log

cards.title: Data design: ranking and feed (PRD v4)
items: PostgreSQL is the only database; Redis is a cache that can be rebuilt from it
Rank score: a column on each profile, recalculated by the worker after every review; index on (category, district, rank_score DESC)
Leaderboards: materialized view ranked per category and district, refreshed concurrently by the worker; top-N copied to Redis sorted sets
Feed: built on read from followed organisers, keyset pagination; trending posts in a Redis sorted set (score proposed)
Likes and views counted in Redis, written to PostgreSQL in batches; the like itself goes straight to PostgreSQL
Tools: Prisma schema and migrations own every table; DBeaver for queries only; dbdiagram.io for the ER diagram
Later if needed: Meilisearch or Typesense for search, pgvector for recommendations

cards.title: Reviews and trust
items: Organiser and provider reviews unlock on a completed booking or a confirmed stall
Attendee reviews unlock from a 'Going' mark made before the event, once it ends
Worker closes review windows after 14 days and recomputes rank scores
Verification documents are private Cloudinary files, opened by admins only through signed links (PDPA)

cards.title: Out of scope
items: Ticketing: tiers, seats, RSVP tickets, QR entry, refunds
Payment gateway: hiring and stall fees are paid outside the app
Google Maps directions to the venue: still under discussion
